newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita withdraws management options plan.
newsitem.headline: Merita withdraws management options plan.

text.p: The board of Finnish banking group Merita Oy decided on Thursday to withdraw a proposal to the annual general meeting for an options scheme for its top management, Merita said in a statement.
"The board found that in the situation that has arisen, the overall interest of the group required a withdrawal of the proposal," Merita said. It did not elaborate.

On Tuesday, Finnish media reported that the Finance Ministry, representing the Finnish state, which is Merita's biggest owner, had demanded changes to the management options scheme unveiled on February 25.

Since it announced the proposal, Merita has come under strong criticism for allegedly trying to line the pockets of top executives before repaying state support granted by the government during the banking crisis in the early 1990s.
The proposal was for a 1.70 million markka options scheme targetted at about 100 management-level employees. The warrants would have entitled holders to subscribe at most 17.0 million Merita shares.

Subscriptions could have been made between March 1, 2000 and March 31, 2003 at a subscription price, which would have been the weighted average price of Merita's A share on the Helsinki bourse between March 10-14, 1997, Merita said.
At 1650/1450 GMT, Merita A traded at 18.90 markka, down 0.10 markka on Wednesday's close.
Merita's annual general meeting will be held on March 18. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
